title: Task & evidence contract
summary: Make the expected outcome, inputs, permissions, verification, and limits explicit.

sections.label: Required fields
items: Task identity, owner, desired outcome and exclusions.
Relevant input and source versions. Include repository and dependency revisions when the task changes or inspects code.
Acceptance criteria, required checks and expected evidence.
Applicable time, correction, tool-call or spending limits, with units and a stopping outcome.
Expected outputs and conditions requiring clarification or assistance.

sections.label: Completion record
sections.text: Keep observed facts, inferences, unresolved questions, executed checks and exceptions distinct. A relevant change requires a review of which earlier checks or approvals still apply. Preserve the earlier evidence as history.

sections.label: Reusable across workflows
sections.text: The same structure can describe a code investigation, document review or data curation task. Each adds its own acceptance criteria. A repository, model call or automated write is not required for every task.

sections.label: Gap review: workflow use and checks
items: Recommended use: Define a task's outcome, boundaries and evidence, then compare the completion record with those terms.
Record input versions, owner, required outputs and checkable acceptance.
Keep executed checks, inferred conclusions and unrun checks distinct in the completion record.
Workflow placement and checks are Atlas recommendations. Existing examples, tenant availability, older product claims and comparative benefits were not revalidated by this mapping review.

sections.label: Gap review: verified source contribution
sections.text: NIST AI RMF Measure calls for documented evaluation methods, metrics and test sets, including uncertainty and limitations of generalization. This scoped source fact was checked on 15 October 2026. The guide's broader workflow and examples remain Atlas proposals, not demonstrated outcomes.

catalog.applicability: Use when handing a task to a person, an agent or a system and the outcome, inputs, permitted actions, checks and limits must be explicit. The same structure fits a code investigation, a document review or a data curation task.
catalog.limits: Reading a topic does not configure tools, execute a workflow or establish passing evidence.
